body: Compute accounts for 58 percent of total cloud spend over the trailing twelve months, storage for 19 percent, data transfer for 9 percent, and observability tooling for 8 percent. Total spend grew 22 percent year over year while provisioned compute capacity grew 31 percent, which means unit efficiency declined even as the bill rose. Compute spend concentrated in three services that together represent almost half of the compute total. Any serious cost program should start with those three services before spreading effort thin.
title: Cloud spend by category, trailing twelve months

body: Median CPU utilization across the production fleet was 21 percent over the last 90 days, and the 25th percentile instance ran below 8 percent. Memory utilization ran higher than CPU, with a median of 47 percent, which suggests instances are sized for memory rather than compute. Roughly one instance in five showed peak utilization below 15 percent across the entire window. These percentiles indicate substantial rightsizing headroom concentrated in the oldest instance families.
title: Fleet utilization percentiles, last 90 days

body: The support organization handled 48,200 tickets last quarter. Password and account access issues made up 27 percent of volume, billing questions 18 percent, and order status 12 percent. Average first response time was 3.1 hours against a target of 4 hours, so responsiveness is not the problem; volume concentration is. The top three categories are all candidates for self-service deflection because they follow predictable resolution scripts.
title: Support ticket volume by category, last quarter

body: Accounts in the lowest usage quartile churned at 9.4 percent per quarter, compared with 1.8 percent for the highest usage quartile. Churn rose sharply in the cohort whose weekly active usage fell by more than half between consecutive months. Renewal outreach that began 45 days before the renewal date retained measurably more at-risk accounts than outreach begun 10 days out. Price was cited in only 14 percent of churn exit surveys, behind product fit and missing integrations.
title: Churn rate by usage cohort, last two quarters

body: Average supplier lead time across component classes was 24 days, but the standard deviation was 11 days, and the worst class swung between 9 and 61 days. Safety stock spending concentrated in the two highest-variance classes, which together hold 63 percent of buffer inventory value. Lead time variance, not average lead time, explains most of the quarter-over-quarter change in inventory carrying cost. Reducing variance in the worst class by a quarter would free more working capital than renegotiating its unit price.
title: Supplier lead time variance by component class

body: Tier one services met their 99.95 percent availability target in ten of the last twelve months. Tier two services targeted 99.9 percent and achieved 99.87 percent, a small miss driven by two incidents in one month. Non-critical internal tools ran at 99.5 percent against no formal target, which the reliability review judged acceptable and not worth further investment. Availability spending reviews concluded that the next dollar is better spent on change safety than on additional redundancy.
title: Availability versus SLO target by service tier
